In this paper, we present a family of five hybrid deep learning models for BUS image classification based on BUSI dataset, which gradually evolves from two-branch integration towards a novel Mask-Guided Cross-Attention (MGCA) scheme. Early and precise diagnosis is the most crucial aspect when talking about enhancing patient outcomes because survival chances fall dramatically depending on the stage of the disease. Among all the various approaches to detecting this disease, breast ultrasound imaging stands out for being a popular, non-invasive, cheap, and timely method especially in patients with dense breast tissue, which makes mammography less effective [2]. Images acquired through this technique can be classified into three major categories: benign, malignant, and normal images. Often the edges of a mass are not clearly delineated on BUS images, coupled with acoustic shadowing, speckle interference, and non-uniform tissue backgrounds, making visual analysis difficult. In breast ultrasound data, where the actual segmentation masks of lesions in benchmark datasets like BUSI are known, there exists potential for exploiting medically informed feature selection in the feature-level fusion step [3],[10]. Conclusion From Literature Survey CNN-only models have inherent structural drawbacks. Research employing only CNN-based feature extraction [5] achieves good local texture classification capability but lacks the ability to model long-distance spatial relationships, leading to poor dete

xture classification capability but lacks the ability to model long-distance spatial relationships, leading to poor detection of overlapping benign and malignant lesions in BUS data sets. Hybrid models therefore represent an important research direction. Dual-branch CNN+Transformer hybrids outperform single-branch baselines. The combination of CNN-local features and Vision Transformers' global features in research [1],[2] has been shown to yield performance gains compared to using either method separately in ultrasound and other similar medical image analysis problems. The use of ground truth segmentation masks in BUSI is poorly exploited. Proposed Methodology A. Overview The present work investigates five hybrid deep learning-based models for the automatic classification of images from a breast ultrasound image dataset called BUSI. All five models share a common dual-branch design: a local feature extractor (a pretrained EfficientNet-B4) and a global context encoder (ViT-B/16 pretrained on ImageNet-21k). The first model EfficientNet-B4 and ViT fuse the two branch outputs via concatenation followed by fully connected classification layers, establishing strong baselines for the 3-class problem (Ben

catenation followed by fully connected classification layers, establishing strong baselines for the 3-class problem (Benign, Malignant, Normal). The remaining four models introduce a novel Mask-Guided Cross-Attention (MGCA) module that replaces simple concatenation with a structured cross-attention mechanism, where the CNN/EfficientNet spatial feature map serves as the Query (Q) and the ViT patch token sequence serves as the Key (K) and Value (V). A ground truth segmentation mask, available for every BUSI sample, guides this cross-attention by suppressing background query positions (setting logits to −∞) so that only tumour-region positions actively query global ViT context.
